doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Hitting bottom and rejoining the Air Force
summary: After work dries up in Philadelphia and Atlantic City he re-enlists and resolves to become the world's greatest bass player.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So you entered into your Philadelphia kind of time from there is that right?

Yeah. Well no, that’s another story. That’s another story. A week in Philadelphia and then I went to Atlantic City for a while, and then there was no more work. I says now what’s happening. I began to assess myself and I said well what’s happening. I says you do have a skill, you can play the tuba, you had a military career, well three or four years anyway, and I says you’re young and all those kinds of things. I says it’s time for you to do something. I hit rock bottom there as far as employment goes. And I’d see all these prosperous looking people and I says there’s nothing out here that I know how to do. What can I do? But there for a short time I did get a job in a haberdashery for about six months. And that had me going for a while. I substituted for a saxophone player. So between those two gigs, working a little bit at nights and the haberdashery, I was able to make it. But after that everything was — you know, because I had to live from day to day. So I decided, I says well I think I’ll go back into the Air Force. So finally that was my decision. I went back in the Air Force and I went back in this time with one stripe. Before I had no stripes. But I had one stripe. I went into the band, the guys had heard that I had worked a week with Ella or had worked with a few musicians around Boston you know, and I had a little prestige there.

Yeah, and had a little tuba experience because I had done that before. So I was a little bit ahead of the game. But I said I have to really do something about my abilities. I says, I decided right there and then that I was going to become the world’s greatest bass player. I decided, that’s what I put into my head. I says you have to do it. I don’t know why, I think I was sort of like driven and I had experienced hunger, and I experienced the disappointments and all those kind of things. And I had a craving or a love, and then all these social things that I experienced before were coming through. You know what I mean? From what I experienced as a child. I didn’t know what they were, but I had to express all of this in some way, otherwise it would have come out in the form of pimples
